transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-17 16:00 UTC
Duration: 42m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Ruiz (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (OrionWorks Head of Search), Liam O'Neill (OrionWorks Platform), Sara Gomez (OrionWorks CTO)
Links shared: https://redwood.share/pilot-deck-orionworks (deck), https://redwood.bench/orionworks-1k (benchmark spreadsheet)

Summary: Quick discovery focused on where to host embeddings/rerank (hosted vs dedicated vs private), throughput shaping, embedding dimensionality tradeoffs, and vector DB integration options. Customer cares about P95 latency < 120ms, 500-1,000 qps fanout, data residency EU, and SOC2 compliance.

Topics: hosting modes, quantized embeddings, KV cache and prefix caching, hybrid-search (ANN + rerank), vector DB placement, throughput dimensioning, SSO/KMS, rollout timeline

Transcript body:
00:00 Maya: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we just have 40 minutes, quick intros then jump into the workload and goals, I'm Maya from Redwood, AE.
00:08 Priya: Hi all, Priya here, we own search at OrionWorks. We wanted to talk through a pilot for embeddings+rerank across our storefront and docs. Main ask is to evaluate hosting options and cost/latency tradeoffs.
00:20 Sara: Hi, Sara here - I'm the CTO, I'll be sizing security / compliance bar.
00:25 Ethan: Ethan Ruiz, solutions eng, I'll try to map the topology options to your qps and tail-latency needs.
00:34 Liam: Liam - infra, will be implementing the pilot if we move forward.
00:40 Maya: Great, quick qual: what's current stack for vectors?
00:45 Priya: We're on Postgres for vectors today (yeah, I know), moving to Milvus in a few teams, we prototype with OpenAI embeddings. Typical query load today is spiky - peak 600 qps sustained for short bursts, average 120 qps.
01:08 Ethan: Ok, and what's the fanout you plan for retrieval? Are you doing 10-50 topk then rerank or wide fanout?
01:15 Priya: We do 50 candidate recall then rerank with our transformer re-ranker. But the ecom team is experimenting with 200 candidate fanout for personalized ranking experiments.
01:26 Maya: Success criteria? Cost per query, p95 latency under 120ms for user facing, and determinism of results for audits. Any compliance needs?
01:36 Sara: SOC2 required, EU data residency for customer data, and we need KMS integration. We also want audit logs for token-level traces.
01:44 Ethan: Good to know, Redwood Private can be deployed in your VPC with customer-managed KMS, audit logs shipped to your SIEM, Dedicated gives isolation but runs in our infra, and Hosted is fastest to get started. There's typically a tradeoff: hosted lowest time-to-value; private gives most control.
02:05 Liam: For throughput, we need to know per-token cost and also how batching/kv cache helps. If we rerank on Redwood model, what's typical throughput for 1k qps?
02:18 Ethan: Real numbers depend on model dim and quantization. For a 1536-d embedding at fp16 on our Dedicated infra you can get ~1k embed qps on an 8xA100 cluster with batching. But if you quantize to int8 and use 768-d smaller model, that jumps a lot. We can run a smoke hosted test to give a concrete number.
02:40 Priya: Our index size today ~12M vectors at 512 dims, but per-customer corpora vary. We also plan sharding across regions for EU residency.
02:54 Maya: That helps. On hybrid search: you mentioned doing ANN in VDB and then reranking - where should rerank live? Close to the vector DB for lower data egress or colocated with model serving for lower output latency?
03:10 Ethan: Exactly the tradeoff. Option A: run ANN in your Milvus/managed VDB (you keep index) and call Redwood Hosted/Dedicated to compute embeddings + rerank. You pay egress/latency for each candidate transfer. Option B: move ANN into a managed vector index on Redwood side (we can host your index in Dedicated) and we do rerank locally which reduces cross-network hops. Option C: Private deploy everything in your VPC so data stays in-region with no egress.
03:40 Liam: Egress is a big cost for us, especially with high fanout. We prefer fewer cross-region roundtrips.
03:47 Ethan: In practice we reduce fanout with a smart hybrid approach: small ANN top-k (e.g., 50) plus a rerank that uses cached prefixes and a lightweight re-encoder to avoid moving full doc text. Also prefix/KV cache for repeated queries cuts cost.
04:05 Priya: What about embedding dimensionality? 512 vs 1536 - accuracy improvements vs cost?
04:12 Ethan: 512 dims are often a sweet spot for reranking setups; 1536 helps recall for some corpora but costs more storage and slower ANN recall. We recommend an eval across your top-100 queries with multiple dims and quantized variants.
04:28 Maya: Any folks asking about quantized embeddings impacting downstream reranker?
04:31 Priya: Yes. Our re-ranker expects fairly precise similarity scores. We worry about degradation if embeddings are lossy.
04:40 Ethan: We've seen quantization (int8 or int4) can be fine for retrieval when you retrain or calibrate; but for tight rerank metrics you'd want higher fidelity. We can run side-by-side evals — Redwood Optimize can output expected recall curves and token economics.
04:59 Sara: On compliance, how is audit logging surfaced? We need immutable logs with user-scoped operations for audits.
05:07 Ethan: Private and Dedicated both support audit logs to your SIEM via secure forwarding. Hosted gives tenant-level logs and we can expose aggregated token traces; for PCI/regulated you should pick Private.
05:22 Priya: Timeline: we want a pilot in dev by mid-Oct and production by EOY if results look good.
05:29 Maya: Sounds reasonable. Quick pricing question: for a 3-month pilot targeting 200 qps sustained with 600 qps bursts, is hosted cheaper?
05:38 Ethan: Hosted is cheapest to start — you pay usage. Dedicated gives predictable unit economics at higher commit levels and may lower cost/throughput if you hit sustained load. Private has higher start-up cost. We'll send a pricing scenario in the SOW.
05:53 Liam: For the bench we want you to test our query mix: 70% short queries, 30% complex long tail. We'll share the query set.
06:02 Priya: Also need to confirm SSO SAML support and RBAC so only search team folks can kick off rerank jobs.
06:10 Ethan: Redwood supports SAML SSO for Private and Dedicated; Hosted supports SSO with a different flow but we can enable RBAC via console.
06:18 Maya: Any questions on integration with Milvus?
06:21 Liam: We'll likely keep Milvus for now. How do you recommend integrating?
06:26 Ethan: There are two patterns: 1) Keep Milvus as the ground truth index, call Redwood for embeddings and rerank; 2) Offload replica indexes to Redwood Dedicated which acts as a cache and can reduce cross-network calls. Pattern 2 reduces egress and tail latency.
06:40 Priya: What about cold start for rerank models, do you warm caches?
06:44 Ethan: We can pre-warm KV caches with top queries and sticky routing. Also shading warm nodes for canary tests.
06:53 Maya: Let's do a concrete pilot scope: 1) Hosted quick eval with sample queries; 2) If latency/egress blow up, test Dedicated with replica index; 3) If compliance requires, scope Private deploy. Does that align?
07:07 Sara: Yes. Make sure the pilot SOW includes acceptance criteria: p95 < 120ms, recall delta < 1% against current baseline, and no EU data egress.
07:18 Ethan: Noted. We'll add those to the SOW.
07:21 Priya: Anything else on cost controls? We want automatic fallback to cheaper models during spikes.
07:27 Ethan: Redwood has routing policies — you can set a cost-based fallback to a smaller model or fallback to cached responses for high load. We'll demo the routing controls in the follow-up.
07:38 Maya: Ok recap / next steps — we'll share pilot SOW and pricing, Ethan will run hosted benchmark, customer to share query set and index stats. Schedule a 30m pilot kickoff next week?
07:52 Priya: Yes let's tentatively schedule for 2026-09-22.
07:57 Sara: We'll loop in compliance and security folks after we get the SOW.
08:03 Maya: Thanks all, we'll follow up in email with links.

Transcript notes: occasional ASR glitches: 'k v cache' transcribed as 'k v cash' in places; speaker labels occasionally generic. Some technical terms abbreviated (ANN, VDB, KMS).

End of call.
